title: Sable and the Archive
premise: Felix Joubert has spent eleven years alone tending the Sable Archive, Earth's last seed vault and cryogenic repository, keeping its beacon lit for a humanity that scattered to the outer colonies and never looked back. When a nine-second gravity flicker reveals that the flicker originated from her own station's hidden second archive—a duplicate vault built by her long-dead mother, containing a rival set of sleepers—Felix learns the colonies are finally coming home, and their arrival protocols will purge one archive to power the other. Torn between the colonists' claim, the sleeping thousands her mother chose, and the handful of sleepers Felix herself has secretly curated over the years, she must decide which half of humanity wakes. In the end, Felix refuses the binary: she burns her own life support to merge both archives into one waking cycle, dying as the beacon-keeper but living on in the first generation born from every branch of the human family tree.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is a former botanist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds before turning to fiction full-time. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction from a farmhouse in Wales, where she keeps her own small seed library.

chapters.title: The Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Felix. During a routine maintenance walk through the seed vaults, gravity stutters for exactly nine seconds, scattering Felix and her tools across the corridor. Alone, she logs the anomaly and discovers it didn't come from outside—it pulsed outward from her own station. Emotional beat: unease breaking through comfortable solitude.

chapters.title: Beacon-Keeper's Almanac
chapters.summary: POV Felix, with flashbacks. We learn Felix's daily rituals, her radio silence with the colonies, and her secret habit of quietly adding sleeper pods to an 'unofficial' wing of the archive—people she rescued from derelict ships. Emotional beat: tenderness disguised as procedure; loneliness made visible.

chapters.title: The Second Vault
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Following the pulse's origin, she finds a sealed sub-level her maps never showed: a duplicate archive built by her mother, Dr. Amara Joubert, holding forty thousand sleepers chosen by the old geneticist's own criteria. A countdown terminal reads 61 days until 'Consolidation.' Emotional beat: betrayal and awe entwined.

chapters.title: Mother's Criteria
chapters.summary: POV Felix reading Amara's logs. Her mother selected sleepers for 'optimal reconstitution'—health, genius, compliance—and dismissed Felix herself as too stubborn to include. Felix realizes the Consolidation will purge her unofficial wing to power the mother-archive's awakening. Emotional beat: grief curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: Signal Home
chapters.summary: POV alternating Felix and Ilsa Voss, a colony fleet navigator. Felix breaks eleven years of silence to warn the colonies about the flicker; instead of thanks, she receives notice that the fleet arrives in fifty days and will execute Consolidation automatically. Emotional beat: the crushing discovery that invisibility was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, then Felix. Over weeks of delayed transmissions, Felix and Ilsa form a wary intimacy—Ilsa feeding her fleet secrets, Felix confessing the three archives. Ilsa reveals the colonies are dying out there and see the vaults as inheritance they're owed. Emotional beat: love kindling inside an impossible conflict.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Dream
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She walks the rows of both archives, listening to dream-recordings of sleepers from each: her mother's chosen, her own rescues, the colonists' ancestors. She understands all three groups are the same species making the same plea. Emotional beat: compassion dissolving the categories she's been fighting over.

chapters.title: Sabotage of the Heart
chapters.summary: POV Felix. With nineteen days left, Felix attempts to rewrite Consolidation but the system requires two authorized keys: hers and her mother's dead biometric signature—which only the archive itself can resurrect. Meanwhile Ilsa warns the fleet command suspects her leaks. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Consolidation Day
chapters.summary: POV Felix and Ilsa. The fleet arrives; Ilsa stalls the boarding party while Felix feeds her own vitals into the system as the second key, authorizing a merged awakening sequence that draws power from the beacon—her life support. The gravity flickers again, nine seconds, as both archives begin to wake together. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into choice.

chapters.title: First Light, First Harvest
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, months later. The merged generation wakes—mother's chosen, Felix's rescued, colonists' kin—tended by Ilsa and the first children born aboard. They plant seeds from every vault under a rebuilt beacon, and Ilsa reads Felix's final log aloud: 'Keep the light on for everyone.' Emotional beat: mourning braided with inheritance fulfilled.
